answer: In an agent market for orchard fruit, trellis repairs, and meadow mowing, each seller must lock a $100 bond for 30 days before accepting work; proven non-delivery burns the bond. Creating new names cannot reuse locked funds, so operating 1,000 fake sellers ties up $100,000, and cheating risks losing it. The rule does not prove identities are unique; it makes each active fake identity consume scarce capital.
